pr.title: Install a release without a clone: the release installer, and field upgrade for release installs (install.md chunk 3)
pr.head: ce42ef93a50d0df161aec8ce9d66a56bb7a7d850

summary: Field is a command-line music tool whose field command and audio daemon, field-audiod, are built from source on your machine, because Field publishes no binaries. Until now the only installer was install.sh in a clone: it built that checkout and linked it onto your PATH with pnpm. This pull request lets you install Field without a clone:

Run outside a git checkout, install.sh now installs a release. It reads the version that package.json names at v0, a tag the Release workflow moves to each new release. It downloads GitHub's archive of that version's own tag, vX.Y.Z, which never moves, into ~/.local/share/field/<version>/. It builds there, sets up again the model workers the old version had, and only then points the current link at the new version. A short shim script, ~/.local/bin/field, runs whatever current names, so an upgrade relinks nothing. field upgrade now tells the two kinds of install apart: a checkout runs its own install.sh, and a release install downloads the newest one and runs that.

Three reviews have read this pull request, and every finding is fixed at this head. The first, at 830f3ab, found four. Offline, field upgrade now runs the installed version's own installer. A failed install removes what it built. field upgrade --help names both installers. And the installer refuses a release from before release installs, such as 0.2.0. The second found that prune deleted any X.Y.Z directory in a shared data directory. The installer now lists, replaces, and removes only directories it can show it made: an X.Y.Z directory whose install.sh carries the shim's marker, or a .download-X.Y.Z holding unpacked/. Anything else in the way stops it before it changes anything.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Checkout install: a git clone whose install.sh builds it in place and links it with pnpm add -g.
  • Release install: a version unpacked from GitHub's tag archive into the data directory and built there.
  • Data directory: ~/.local/share/field by default, holding one directory per version, current, the shared JUCE cache, and release.conf.
  • current: a relative symlink naming the version field runs. Only a successful install switches it.
  • Shim: the script in ~/.local/bin/field that runs current/dist/cli.js.
  • release.conf: the repository, ref, and bin directory an install follows, so a fork keeps upgrading from the fork.
  • Workers: optional Python model environments, each in python/<worker>/.venv inside a version.

cards.title: What a release install does, in order
cards.html:
1. Refuse in a Windows shell. Check prerequisites: Node 24, pnpm, CMake 3.24 or newer, curl, and tar, that ~/.local/bin/field is free or already the shim, and that the bin directory can be written.
  2. Read the version at the ref and accept only X.Y.Z.
  3. Download and unpack the tag archive beside the versions, check it holds one directory whose package.json names that version and whose install.sh writes the shim, and move it into place.
  4. Build the CLI, the UI, and the daemon.
  5. Set up again, with the new CLI, each worker set up in the old version.
  6. Rename a new link over current, write the shim and release.conf, and remove every version but the new one and the one it replaced.

A failure in steps 1 to 5 leaves the old version current, and an exit trap says so and removes what it built of the new one.

cards.title: What the change leaves for later
cards.html:
• A Windows installer, handed to windows-portability.md §7.2. field upgrade refuses on Windows.
  • Serving the installer from field.one, which is chunk 4.
  • A real install from GitHub and a run on Linux. The author tested end to end on macOS against file:// stand-ins.

groups.title: The release installer
groups.kicker: install.sh gains a release mode beside its checkout mode
intro: install.sh decides its mode from where it runs. A checkout is the script inside a git work tree, with src/cli.ts beside it. Anything else installs a release: bash reading the script from curl, the copy field upgrade downloads to a temporary directory, and a release version's own copy, which has the source but no .git.

The release path is new code from release_init down. It is written for a script piped from curl. Every command is inside a function and main "$@" is the last line, so a download cut short runs nothing. It changes what field runs only with one rename at the end, after everything that can fail has succeeded.

checks.text: A truncated pipe runs nothing: before main, the script only assigns variables. Piped into bash 3.2, BASH_SOURCE is empty, so a piped run never takes the checkout path. I checked both by piping a stub into /bin/bash.

files.note: The whole release path: where installs live, the download and its checks, the switch, the shim, pruning, and the release status rows.

checks.text: The data directory comes from FIELD_DATA_DIR first. Without it, a version's own copy uses the parent of its directory when a current link sits there, and anything else uses the XDG data directory. FIELD_REPO and FIELD_REF come ahead of release.conf, and both are held to the characters GitHub allows before they go into a URL.

The inference trusts any current link. A release unpacked as field-0.2.0/ beside another program's current link installs there and repoints that link, though it deletes nothing. The review suggests inferring only when the script's own directory is named X.Y.Z.

GITHUB_TOKEN reaches curl through its configuration on standard input, never on the command line, and only for GitHub's own hosts over HTTPS. A host such as github.com.example.com does not match the pattern.
v0 moves, so the installer reads only the version from it. The archive comes from the version's own tag, which does not move, and the version must be X.Y.Z because it becomes a directory name.

Only a directory named X.Y.Z whose install.sh carries the shim's marker counts as a version. In a test harness copy, a first install into a data directory holding 3.11.4/bin/python3 and notes/ left both, and printed no removed row.
A field in the bin directory that is not the shim, or a bin directory nobody can write, stops the install before anything changes, because the shim is written after the switch.

A directory of someone else's where the version or its download would go stops the install with exit status 69. I checked both a foreign 0.2.0/ and a .download-0.2.0/ without unpacked/; each was left intact.

A release from before release installs has an install.sh without the shim marker, and its own field upgrade could never move off it, so the installer refuses it before anything builds. v0.2.0's install.sh carries no marker, and a test covers the refusal.
The switch renames a new link over current with rename(2) through node. mv would move the new link into the directory the old link names, and ln -sfn removes the old link before making the new one.

A failed install removes the new version only when it is a Field version and not the one current names, and its download only when it is Field's. After a failed daemon build, no 0.3.0/ is left and status prints no previous row.

current switches only after the download, the builds, and the worker setup succeed. A failing setup_workers_again at the end of an || list still stops the script under set -e; I checked that in bash 3.2.

files.note: Reads FIELD_FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR into CMake's cache as FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR, so every release version shares one JUCE download.

checks.text: Only a release install sets the variable. A checkout, and CI, leave it unset, so their JUCE stays under build/_deps as before. It is an environment variable because pnpm build:native passes no -D.

groups.title: field upgrade for release installs
groups.kicker: field upgrade picks an installer by the kind of install
intro: field upgrade [target] runs an installer with the same target and passes its exit status through. In a checkout it runs the checkout's own install.sh, as before. In a release install it downloads the newest install.sh at the ref release.conf records, because the copy inside an installed version is as old as that version, and runs it with FIELD_DATA_DIR set to the data directory it found from its own real path. Under FIELD_OFFLINE, nothing can download, so it runs the installed version's own copy instead.

files.note: Tells a checkout from a release install, reads release.conf, downloads the installer with curl and runs it with bash, or, offline, runs the installed version's own.

checks.text: The package root is resolved to its real path first, because the shim runs current/dist/cli.js, and the data directory is the parent of the version directory, not of the link.

Under FIELD_OFFLINE a release install downloads nothing and runs <version>/install.sh with FIELD_DATA_DIR set, so status reaches its offline row. I called the built upgrade('status') with FIELD_OFFLINE=1 against a throwaway data directory to check it.

files.note: The field upgrade help and the comment above it now say which installer each kind of install runs.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The real install.sh under real bash, with stand-ins for everything it calls
intro: src/install.test.ts runs the real install.sh with a temporary HOME and a PATH that holds only stand-ins for pnpm, cmake, curl, and the CLI, plus links to the ordinary tools. The curl stand-in serves GitHub from local files and fails for any other host. Releases are cut as the Release workflow cuts them, with a git archive of each tag. src/commands/upgrade.test.ts serves stand-in installers from file:// URLs.

files.note: Both install modes, every release status row, and each failure leaving the old version current.

checks.text: Every test is synchronous, so vitest's worker never read its task-update replies and timed out after the file passed. This one-turn yield after each test lets the reply in, and the 30-second timeout at the top covers a test that runs the installer several times.
pnpm exec vitest run src/install.test.ts src/commands/upgrade.test.ts src/release.test.ts passed 111 tests in 3 files with no unhandled errors at this head.

files.note: The installer download at the recorded ref, overrides ahead of the record, and the token going only to GitHub.

groups.title: Documentation and plans
groups.kicker: The README and manuals lead with the one-line install, and the plan records chunk 3
intro: The README and docs/cli.md now lead with the curl install and treat a checkout as the way to work on Field itself. docs/install.md gains a section for each part of a release install: where it lives, upgrading, workers, the targets, following a fork, and removing it. The install plan records chunk 3 as built, decides worker setup across versions (§7.5) and Windows (§7.6), and hands a Windows installer to windows-portability.md §7.2.

files.note: Leads with the curl install. The checkout install moves under "To work on Field itself".
The install section, the FIELD_OFFLINE, FIELD_REPO, and data-directory variables, and the field upgrade row.
The user's guide to both kinds of install, each target, and each status row.

checks.text: The pin example now names vX.Y.Z and says the installer refuses a release from before release installs, such as 0.2.0. A new paragraph asks you to give FIELD_DATA_DIR a directory of Field's own and says what the installer writes and removes there.

files.note: Says the release installer follows v0 now, and links the user's guide.
§3.2 as built, two decisions, the chunk 3 criteria, and §10 on what building it found and how it was verified.

checks.text: The plan stays in-progress. §3.2 step 5 now says what the installer removes in a data directory that holds other things, §4 records the decision on pinning to an exact tag, and the only open question, §7.4 on which domain serves the installer, belongs to chunk 4.
